definition: Celebratory means relating to or marking a celebration; festive in purpose.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word celebratory. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know celebratory should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The whole block turned out for a celebratory cookout the weekend the new park finally opened.
Cheerful describes any pleasant mood, but celebratory ties the good mood to a specific occasion being marked.
Jubilant is stronger than celebratory — not just marking an occasion, but exulting in it with open, triumphant joy.

Congratulatory means expressing praise for a specific achievement, and it is aimed at the achiever -- a congratulatory card, call, or handshake speaks directly to the person who did it. Celebratory belongs to the event: it marks the occasion with festivity. You send a congratulatory note; you throw a celebratory dinner.

Joyous means full of happiness -- it names the emotion itself, wherever it appears. Celebratory is about purpose, not feeling: a thing is celebratory because it exists to mark a win, a launch, a milestone. A joyous morning needs no occasion at all; a celebratory toast without an occasion makes no sense.

The robotics team had eaten in the same quiet corner of the cafeteria all year.

But the Monday after their machine finally cleared the qualifying round, their table looked different: someone had brought a grocery-store cake, someone else had tied a single balloon to a chair, and the coach gave a toast with a juice box.
It was a small lunch, but an unmistakably celebratory one — every detail existed to mark the win.
The cake, balloon, and toast all exist specifically to mark the team's win, which is what makes the lunch celebratory rather than just cheerful.
neutral; describes events, gestures, and atmospheres
